channel.title: Ride The Andes — Journal
channel.description: Field notes from Colombia's cycling heartland — climb profiles, route guides, altitude advice and stories from Boyacá, by the team behind Ride The Andes.

item.title: Why Colombia Produces the World’s Best Climbers
item.description: Altitude, gradient and a century of cycling culture — the real reasons Boyacá and the Colombian altiplano keep producing Grand Tour climbers.

item.title: Villa de Leyva by Bike: Colonial Roads
item.description: Routes, seasons and practicalities for cycling around Villa de Leyva — the desert loop through Santa Sofía, and what the cobbles do to a road bike.

item.title: The Tota Ascent: Colombia's Highest Lake
item.description: Gradient, altitude, surface and pacing for the climb around Lago de Tota — Colombia's largest lake at 3,015 m, and the queen stage of the Boyacá Traverse.

item.title: Is It Safe to Cycle in Colombia?
item.description: What's outdated, what genuinely requires care, and how we keep international riders safe across rural Boyacá — by people who ride these roads every week.

item.title: Cycling at Altitude in Colombia
item.description: How to arrive from sea level and ride well above 2,500 m in Boyacá — what happens to your body, the first 72 hours, and the warning signs that matter.

item.title: Riding All 123 Municipalities of Boyacá
item.description: Two riders, 123 municipalities, thirteen months. What Diego Supelano's Reto 123 taught us about Colombia's cycling heartland — and why it became Ride The Andes.
